extraction.name: SeamlessAlign
extraction.description: SeamlessAlign is the largest open dataset for multimodal translation, totaling 470,000 hours of automatically aligned speech translations across 37 languages, created through parallel data mining using a multimodal embedding space.
extraction.creator: Seamless Communication, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Parallel data mining was employed to create SeamlessAlign. Starting with a large collection of raw audio, files were chunked into overlapping segments and speech Language Identification (LID) was applied. On the text side, sentence-segmented data from NLLB was used. Speech and text corpora were projected into a common embedding space, in which mining was performed to identify translation pairs with optimal segmentation. Audio was deduplicated, downloaded, resampled at 16KHz, and filtered for non-speech data using an audio event detection model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Non-speech data was filtered out using a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model. Audio longer than 30 seconds was filtered out because the SONAR encoders were not trained on long audio.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data (approximately 1 million hours in English), and sentence-segmented text data from NLLB covering multiple languages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: XSTS protocol for semantic similarity evaluation of S2TT and S2ST tasks; MOS protocol for naturalness/quality of S2ST audio. Annotators evaluated source-target audio pairs for semantic similarity on a scale, with practice evaluations before annotation. Non-speech tags were to be ignored. For items with annotator disagreement of 2 or more score values, 2 additional annotators evaluated the same item.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Calibration using a monolingual 'cross-lingual calibration set' with 'moderated calibration' methodology to reduce language-level annotator biases. Annotator crews sufficiently 'out of calibration' could be identified and excluded. The calibration process was found to improve correlation with automatic metrics.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item by default; 5 annotators for items where the initial 3 annotators had a disagreement of 2 or more score values
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ETOX for automatic toxicity detection; Whisper-Large-v2 and Whisper-Medium for ASR-BLEU computation; Blaser 2.0 for modality-agnostic quality estimation; MMS-TTS for generating speech from text for bias evaluation
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset and model exhibit gender bias, specifically overgeneralizing to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (average preference of ~10%) and lack of robustness when varying gender (~3%). Different languages show varying distributions of toxic terms across demographic axes (e.g., ability, age, body type, gender, nationality, race/ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class). Some languages show high concentration of toxicity in specific axes (e.g., Bengali 80% socio-economic status, Kyrgyz 94% cultural).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Word list-based toxicity detection (ETOX) has known limitations: (1) over-detection of terms that are only toxic in specific contexts, (2) reliance on precise tokenization which is harder for non-segmenting or highly agglutinative languages, and (3) when used with ASR before lexical matching, tends to produce false negatives especially for non-English languages. Gender bias detection using noun lists is limited by reliance on linguistic gender clues as a proxy, and results from a limited set of 30 nouns may not generalize to all other noun sets.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to promote accessibility and bridge the gap in direct speech translation across many languages. It could adversely impact user experiences through added toxicity and gender bias in translation outputs. The authors document these effects to motivate future mitigation efforts and open-source all contributions to ensure researchers with limited computing resources can use the work.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes demographic descriptors across axes such as ability, age, body type, characteristics, cultural background, gender and sex, nationality, political ideologies, race/ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, and socioeconomic class, as reflected in the HolisticBias evaluation dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset (SeamlessAlign, 470,000+ hours) is intended for training and evaluating massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation systems supporting S2ST, T2ST, S2TT, T2TT, and ASR tasks. It is also used for fine-tuning and robustness evaluation. The authors open-source tools to recreate and extend the dataset for further research in speech translation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The models and data tools are open-sourced at https://github.com/facebookresearch/seamless_communication, including model weights, inference code, fine-tuning recipes, and data creation pipelines. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were over-segmented using VAD to create overlapping splits, roughly octupling the number of potential segments. The other datasets were split randomly in 80/20 proportion so that the same source audio or text always goes to the same partition.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text data used the same cleaning and filtering steps from NLLB. Audio data was deduplicated by URL, downloaded, resampled at 16KHz, filtered for non-speech using an audio event detection (AED) model, segmented using Voice Activity Detection (VAD), and language-identified using a speech LID model. Audio longer than 30 seconds was filtered out for BLASER training.
